item.title: Weekly Newsletter #34 — July 14, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #34 · July 14, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🕯️ SUNDAY: MEMORIAL FOR DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This Sunday, join us for a community memorial event to remember the life and legacy of Dr. Barbara Friedes.
We'll meet at 8:30 AM at Barbara's Angel Bike at 18th and Spruce. Please bring a filled reusable water to pour into a symbolic memorial.

🎉 A FEDERAL HOUSING WIN

Good news! The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act is now law!
Though it's not a perfect piece of legislation, it includes important provisions for boosting housing construction and it's a sign that Congress is beginning to take the housing crisis seriously.
Read more in this piece from the Niskanen Center: 3 reasons the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act matters

🍻 HOUSING HAPPY HOUR RECAP

Thank you to everyone who came out to our Housing Happy Hour last week!
We had a great time discussing our ongoing campaigns, including our efforts to fight for more homes near transit, ADU legalization legislation, and a "Golden Girls Law".

🚇 SATURDAY: TRANSPORTATIONCAMP PHL

TransportationCamp PHL's Summer Gathering is this Saturday!
Transportation professionals, students, and advocates will get together for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.
Join them at 11:30 AM at 30th Street Station for the kickoff.
 

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inside Climate News / Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Likely to Punt on Mass Transit Funding—Again

“There is no excuse left for lawmakers. In the year we celebrate 250 years of this great country, let’s fund the system that moves it, and let’s get it done by June 30,” said Dr. Jay Arzu of 5th Square Advocacy, an urbanist group, at the rally. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO? Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

  

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jul 18

TransportationCamp PHL Summer Gathering

11:30 AM Kickoff · Meet at 30th St Station

Join transportation professionals, students, and advocates for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.
Jul 19

Memorial for Dr. Barbara Friedes

8:30 AM to 9:30 AM · 18th and Spruce at Barbara's Angel Bike

Join us in remembering the life of Dr. Barbara Friedes with a community memorial event. Please bring a full reusable water bottle to pour into the symbolic memorial.
Jul 21

Small Developers: Learn How to Work with PHA

3:00 PM to 5:00PM · PHA Headquarters, 2013 Ridge Ave

Small developers, bring your W-9s and MBE/WBE-certifications and get registered with PHA on the spot.
Jul 24

West Market St. Petition Press Rally

11:00 AM to 11:30 AM · 34th and Market

Join us to demand PennDOT implement the safety improvements we called for alongside PBA in our joint West Market St petition. We'll join elected officials in speaking out about the urgent need to implement these changes. Bring your safe streets signs for the media to see!
Jul 27

Book Launch: Routledge Handbook of Urban Design Practice

5:30 PM to 7:00PM · Village of Industry and Art, 320 S Broad St

Attend this book launch featuring a panel discussion with contributors and practitioners working across urban design, planning, landscape architecture, infrastructure, and community development, followed by a book signing and reception at Frankie's Summer Club.
Jul 28

24 Hours on Transit

7:30 AM · City Hall

Transit Forward Philly will be hosting a 24-hour transit marathon to advocate for the buses, trains, trolleys and even bikeshare that keep Philly moving.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

 

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

The Philadelphia Citizen / Adaptive Reuse for Historic Properties is NOT a Loophole

Niskanen Center / 3 reasons the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act matters

City Cast Philly / Could SEPTA Be Your Next Landlord?

Pro-Housing Pittsburgh / New Report: Modernizing Property Tax Assessments in Allegheny County

wcnc.com / North Carolina ends mandatory parking minimums for new developments

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Inquirer.com / The Ben Franklin Bridge turned 100 with thousands of people walking across to celebrate

Inquirer.com / Philly’s public toilets are important in lots of ways. We need more of them.

🚌 TRANSIT

nextcity.org / Philly’s Zero Fare Transit Program Has Been Extended, But Advocates Want More

NBC10 Philadelphia / SEPTA is spending millions to stop fare evasion. Is it paying off?

Inquirer.com / SEPTA cuts 3 daytime trains from Glenside riders for less crowded cars, fewer delays

NBC10 Philadelphia / In pilot program, SEPTA's Fox Chase Regional Rail Station gets new bike lockers

Inside Climate News / Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Likely to Punt on Mass Transit Funding—Again

🚲 MOBILITY

SEPTA

  • Director, ERP Applications
  • Planning Analyst (SP&A)

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #32 — July 2, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #32 · July 02, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏘️ INSIDE OUR CAMPAIGN FOR MORE HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Check out Tuesday’s episode of the City Cast Philly podcast featuring our board member Fae Ehsan in a deep dive into our More Homes Near Transit campaign!

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO?

If you are, we want to know! Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

Don't know what an RCO is? Read this for an explainer and find your RCO here. RCOs play important roles in approving housing and safe streets projects--they're a great way to get directly involved in making your neighborhood a better place to live.

🎉 EXPANDED MARKET ST REDESIGN

Ever since it officially opened last month, we've been huge fans of the newly redesigned Market Street between 2nd and 6th Streets. The freshly installed traffic calming and protected bike lanes make the street much safer and more pleasant to use.

And now, this redesign is headed all the way to City Hall!

The City recently received a $2.5 million federal grant to begin planning work for the portion of Market between 6th and City Hall, and we can't wait to see their new designs.

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📢 FRIDAY: RALLY FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

Pennsylvania needs new revenue sources to keep transit systems moving across the Commonwealth. At this critical moment, transit supporters can take action now to encourage their legislators to create new revenue sources that keep transit moving in every PA community.

Join us this Friday, June 26th, at 10am at the 5th St./Independence Hall L stop for a rally and press conference calling on Harrisburg to fund public transit!

Almost every transit agency across the state is making cuts due to a lack of state funding--we need your help to stop this!

How else can you help?

  1. Sign and share this take action link from our friends at Transit For All PA. It's quick and easy, takes less than two minutes!
  2. Sign up to make a few calls to your legislators on your lunch hour this Thursday.

Join Philly Bike Action's Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar this Saturday! The webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors, followed by a Q&A section.

📈 WHY PEDESTRIAN DEATHS ARE RISING

Despite drops in pedestrian fatalities in peer countries across the world, US pedestrian deaths are up substantially over the past two decades.

Why is the US falling behind? At least part of the answer is our giant trucks and SUVs.

This piece from the New York Times does a great job visualizing how larger vehicles pose a much greater danger to pedestrians on our streets. From larger blind spots, to higher hood heights, crashes are both more likely and more deadly.

The urbanist group 5th Square had been meeting with City Council members in advance of Thursday’s final vote on the bill strengthening transit-oriented development.
...
“The idea that all of the stations will be opted in at once is unlikely,” said Jay Arzu, housing organizer with 5th Square and the founder of the Roosevelt Boulevard Subway Movement.

“They made the intention clear that they’ll look at it on an individual, case-by-case basis, which is disappointing for transit advocates,” Arzu said. “But we recognize it’s another step in the right direction. Sometimes you just got to take what you can get.”
